answer: Use a public randomness beacon to pick a small, unpredictable audit sample each epoch, and let only agents at the zenith of a long, checkable work record enter the draw. An honest agent pays that history cost once. An attacker cannot know which fakes the beacon will name, so each fake must also build a full record, keep it current, and risk losing a deposit when a violet-flagged audit finds copied or hollow work. A thousand sybils thus cost a thousand histories and deposits, while honest agents face only one proportionate audit risk.
